DSMZ producer catalogue recognizes Camphomycin, Carcinomycin, Caryomycin, Phyllomycin, Candimycin and distinct Pluramycin A/B. This supports nomenclature and producer association, not pure molecular identity or interchangeability.
Supplier explicitly gives Collinomycin as alpha-Rubromycin synonym with C27H20O12; matches CHEBI:220350 formula. No molecular property enrichment beyond identity proposed.
Chromomycin A2 is explicitly Aburamycin A, CAS6992-70-7, C59H86O26. Supports CHEBI:202873 and rejects fuzzy Chromomycin A3 candidates.
Supplier explicitly equates Cinerubin A and Cinerubine A; CAS34044-10-5, formula C42H53NO16. Supports same letter-A MeSH target; not R/B/Y congeners.
Original work distinguishes angustmycin A and C and identifies C with psicofuranine. Contradicts current authorizing A=psicofuranin note.

Original Geomycin from Streptomyces xanthophaeus is a basic antibiotic mixture separable as A/B/C/D, demonstrating a non-oxytetracycline sense of the bare name. Modern fungal Geomycin A also cannot be substituted by prefix alone.
Original isolation distinguishes bafilomycin A1,A2,B1,B2,C1,C2; bare source name does not select A1.
Original work distinguishes phoslactomycins A-F with different substituents, so an unspecified graph label cannot identify one congener.

evidence.locator: 2025 original kineomicin research article, section on clade C and azureomycin
evidence.supports_or_contradicts: Authors report azureomycin structure unresolved; genomic association does not identify a purified congener. OLS separately retrieves A and B.
Original Danomycin is an iron-containing polypeptide related to ferrimycin/albomycin; relatedness does not justify exact mapping to them.
Patent distinguishes Danubomycin B components, mixtures and salts; source bare name lacks purification/salt context.
Names achromoviromycin isolated from Streptomyces achromogenes. Supports the source name, not an unobserved molecular structure or a convenient similarly named drug.
Primary literature specifically names Tertiomycin A from Streptomyces albireticuli. Metadata supports historical name existence; no full structure claim is made.

evidence.locator: Umezawa authored antibiotic list with separate Tertiomycin A/B
evidence.supports_or_contradicts: Separate named Tertiomycin A/B entries support retaining the B designation; this list supplies no structure proving external identity.
Culture collection separately lists champamycin A and B; B source qualifier must be retained.
Primary culture collection lists Bandamycin A and B; generic Bandamycin does not identify an individual component.

evidence.locator: DSMZ Strains Producing Special Compounds, Cladomycin entry
evidence.supports_or_contradicts: Culture collection names Cladomycin as produced by Streptomyces lilacinus DSM40254. Not a structural alias for cladosporin.
Original paper separates major destomycin A and minor B; bare source label cannot be promoted to A, C or the differently spelled Destomysin/hygromycin target.
Primary work describes original Eurocidin as A/B mixture and distinguishes Candimycin A. Individual newer Eurocidin congeners are not generic identity matches.
Original Durhamycin is a pentaene antifungal produced by Streptomyces durhamensis. Bare source has no factor/paper linking it to newer Durhamycin A/B ontology hits.
Original research discusses Ascosin from Streptomyces canescus; no source-backed external exact identity follows from related biological mechanism.
Flavensomycinoic acid is only a moiety common to flavensomycin and prasinons; rejects mapping whole Flavensomycin to MeSH flavensomycinoic acid.
Original literature explicitly names Grasseriomycin in silkworm jaundice-virus work; citation establishes legacy name only, not modern chemical structure.
Candimycin and Candicidin are separately enumerated; lexical similarity does not authorize their merge.

Explicitly reports Hitachimycin identified with stubomycin by physicochemical properties despite different production strains; supports exact synonym relation.

evidence.locator: Waksman authored monograph, actinomycin nomenclature passage
evidence.supports_or_contradicts: Historical nomenclature explicitly describes Actinomycin A as a mixture containing I-V; no individual D substitution is justified.
